long_biography.plain_text:
Boca Raton businessman Dick Schmidt drew on Caribbean sailing and flying when he wrote The Boy and the Dolphin, his first novel. Its young protagonist befriends a dolphin and later becomes a naval pilot. Schmidt had served in the Army himself. He described discovering parts of his plots while writing, rather than knowing every development before he sat down at the computer.

His subsequent novels included Memory Road and Career. For his first book, he pledged proceeds from copies purchased through a designated university link to Florida Atlantic University's Kelly Family Scholarship Fund. The fund helps students with financial need finish their degrees.
